lines.text: I was a shell on a string, I was salt in your hand,
I was a stone they rowed home from a faraway land.
Too heavy to steal, so the whole island kept count,
every name, every owner, every stone, every amount.
Then they dug me up as gold from the dark underground,
hard to make, hard to fake, so the whole world came around.
Kings put their faces on me, stamped me and swore,
but a king with a war always wants a little more.
Stroke of a pen, they did it again,
turned all your hours into paper and wind.
They can print the paper, they can't print the proof.
Twenty-one million. That's the truth.
So they clipped off my edges and they cut me with tin,
every emperor swore it would never happen again.
Then in China they printed me, the first fiat to fall,
paper by decree, and it didn't last at all.
Nineteen-twelve, J.P. Morgan said it plain to the man:
"Gold is money. Everything else is credit." Understand?
Thirty-three, bring your gold to the bank by May,
or it's ten years in a cell, and they called it okay.
Seventy-one, Sunday night on TV,
Nixon closed the window and the dollar broke free.
Now the strongest of currencies lost ninety-five percent,
and they call it two percent, like it's rent.
Stroke of a pen, they did it again,
turned all your hours into paper and wind.
They can print the paper, they can't print the proof.
Twenty-one million. That's the truth.
Two-thousand-eight and the big banks shook,
the banks got the bailout, and the savers got took.
Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.
October oh-eight, Satoshi, a name nobody knew,
dropped nine pages, no pitch, no promise, just proof.
Solved the double-spend, took the bank out the middle,
no king and no council to shave me a little.
January oh-nine, Genesis, block zero,
stamped the bailout headline, a receipt, not a hero.
Hal Finney was running it the very next day,
block after block, and it's still ticking away.
Every four years the new coins get cut in half,
twenty-one million, go on, do the math.
Property in cyberspace, keys you can carry,
granite at the bottom, and the rules never vary.
Stroke of a pen, they did it again,
turned all your hours into paper and wind.
They can print the paper, they can't print the proof.
Twenty-one million. That's the truth.
I was a shell. I was gold. I was paper. Now I'm proof.
